Greece, Turkey clash over protected Aegean marine areas
items.description: Turkey has announced the creation of two protected zones in a disputed area of the Aegean Sea, sparking an angry reaction from Greece. Does this mark a new chapter in a long-running dispute between the two countries?

items.title: Niger: Junta says back in control after mutiny
items.description: Gunfire and explosions have been reported in Niger, as mutinying soldiers attempted to storm the presidential palace in the capital, Niamey, in a challenge to the ruling junta. The government said it had regained control after hours of fighting on Saturday. Léo Paichard and Nick Rushworth report.

items.title: Niger junta says it is back in control after attempted coup
items.description: Niamey airport and the presidential palace were targeted on Saturday, as well as the national television station, which went off the air for just over an hour.

items.description: Ahmed Hrustanovic reflects on Ratko Mladic's death with NPR's Scott Simon. All of Hrustanovic's adult male relatives died in the Srebrenica Massacre engineered by Mladic.

items.title: Four children killed as separate attacks in Gaza destroy aid supplies
items.description: Israeli attacks killed four children and destroyed humanitarian aid supplies in what turned out to be a deadly week in war-ravaged Gaza, the UN emergency relief agency, OCHA, said on Friday.

items.description: Local journalists reporting on Sudan’s civil war and humanitarian crisis there are facing a campaign of intimidation by rival military forces.
